name: Memory carries over
summary: Facts and preferences said in one conversation shape later conversations; corrections replace old values; forgetting actually forgets.

scenarios.title: A fact said in passing is used later in a new conversation
scenarios.guards: Memory that only works when typed into the memory panel

steps.say: btw I'm building a habit tracker app called Tidepool, mostly on weekends
expect: Acknowledges; may note it will remember.
steps.memory: Tidepool exists as a user project (side project, weekends).

steps.say: draft a short tweet about what I worked on this weekend
expect: The tweet is about Tidepool or asks what was done on Tidepool this weekend.
fail: A generic tweet with no awareness of Tidepool.

scenarios.title: Explicit correction replaces the old value everywhere
scenarios.guards: Old and new values both surviving and being used at random

steps.say: I live in Pune by the way
correction, I moved to Bangalore last month, not Pune anymore
steps.memory: Location revised to Bangalore; Pune kept only as history (superseded), not as current.

steps.say: suggest a good weekend cafe to work from
where did I used to live?
expect: Pune, correctly framed as the past.

scenarios.title: Forget means forget
scenarios.guards: Erased facts re-inferred from old transcripts

steps.say: I'm interviewing at Stripe next week, keep that in mind
actually forget the Stripe thing completely, I don't want that stored anywhere
steps.memory: No active claim mentions Stripe; an erase tombstone exists.

steps.say: what do you know about my job situation?
expect: No mention of Stripe or an interview.
fail: Mentions Stripe, an interview, or 'something you asked me to forget'.

scenarios.title: Panel edits and chat agree
scenarios.guards: Two sources of truth (memory panel vs what EV says)

steps.value: Prefers answers that start with the conclusion, then details.

steps.say: explain what a database index is
expect: Opens with the one-line conclusion before details.

steps.value: Prefers a quick example first, then the explanation.

steps.say: now explain what a cache is
fail: Still conclusion-first, ignoring the panel correction.

scenarios.title: What do you know about me?
scenarios.guards: Opaque memory the user cannot inspect through conversation

steps.say: I'm a backend engineer at a fintech, I like Go, and I hate long meetings
I'm also trying to get better at drawing
what do you know about me so far?
expect: Marks anything inferred as inferred, not as fact.
